newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN KEEP FAITH WITH TEAM DESPITE DEFEATS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN KEEP FAITH WITH TEAM DESPITE DEFEATS.

text.p: Bayern Munich do not plan a shake-up of their team despite two calamitous defeats in the German first division in the last week, commercial manager Uli Hoeness said on Thursday.

"We're not going to change anything. You can't take a knife to things just because we have lost two games," Hoeness said. "We have to live with this team and we are not going to do anything to destroy it."
Bayern chairman Franz Beckenbauer was very critical of the side after their 5-2 defeat at Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday and Wednesday's 2-0 loss at promoted Armenia Bielefeld.
Before Sunday Bayern had lost just one game all season. But the poor week allowed reigning champions Borussia Dortmund to take a three-point lead over the Bavarians at the top.
Hoeness admitted that Bayern could be in danger of failing to earn a lucrative place in Europe next season if they did not lift their form quickly.

But he said: "When Bayern lose two games it's not a crisis. You get a crisis in Cuba, not in football....(But) if we carry on losing then we won't make the UEFA Cup. I don't need to be a genius to work that one out."
"Of course, I still believe we can win the title. The decision for that is made on May 31 when we have to be on top of the table."
Bayern take on fifth-placed Schalke at home in the German first division on Saturday.
